subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Alkylating agents and platinum compounds: mechanisms, clinical pharmacology, toxicities and resistance

steps.tx: Oxazaphosphorine alkylators **Cyclophosphamide** and ifosfamide represent hepatic prodrugs requiring CYP2B6 bioactivation to active 4-hydroxy metabolites. Intracellular cleavage liberates phosphoramide mustard alongside acrolein, a toxic urothelial metabolite directly responsible for chemical **haemorrhagic cystitis**. Ifosfamide generates substantially greater acrolein and chloroacetaldehyde quantities than cyclophosphamide, creating elevated risks of severe haemorrhagic cystitis and central encephalopathy.

steps.tx: Uroprotective **Mesna** sodium 2-mercaptoethanesulfonate specifically prevents bladder toxicity caused by oxazaphosphorine therapy. Following administration, free thiol groups on mesna bind directly to urotoxic **acrolein** within the urinary tract, synthesizing a non-toxic, stable thioether conjugate that is safely excreted. Co-administration of mesna alongside vigorous intravenous hydration is mandatory during ifosfamide therapy and high-dose cyclophosphamide conditioning regimens.

points: Elevated risk of chronic bladder fibrosis
Not prevented by standard diuretics alone

right.title: Mesna Neutralization

steps.tx: Inorganic coordination complex **Cisplatin** enters tumour cells and undergoes intracellular aquation, reacting with nucleophilic DNA bases. Cisplatin covalently links DNA to form intrastrand guanine-guanine adducts that distort the double helix, inducing **DNA double-strand breaks** and triggering p53-dependent apoptotic death. Key dose-limiting toxicities encompass cumulative nephrotoxicity, high emetogenicity, and bilateral high-frequency sensorineural ototoxicity.

rows: Aggressive pre- and post-hydration with mannitol
Standard outpatient hydration without forced diuresis
Avoid cold exposure; no extensive forced diuresis

steps.tx: Second-generation platinum analog **Carboplatin** possesses a cyclobutanedicarboxylate leaving group that slows aquation kinetics compared to cisplatin. While carboplatin produces equivalent cytotoxic platinum-DNA crosslinks, it features substantially lower nephrotoxic, ototoxic, and emetogenic liabilities. However, carboplatin produces significantly greater myelosuppressive **thrombocytopenia**, requiring precise dosing using the Calvert formula based on target area under the concentration-time curve and creatinine clearance.

steps.tx: **Oxaliplatin** avoids CYP450 metabolism and is cleared non-enzymatically. Renal impairment matters: for creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min a reduced starting dose of 65 mg/m2 is advised. Calcium and magnesium infusions may reduce neurotoxicity. Extravasation requires stopping the infusion and removing the line without flushing.

steps.tx: Third-generation platinum agent **Oxaliplatin** features a bulky 1,2-diaminocyclohexane DACH carrier ligand that forms unique platinum-DNA adducts. These bulky lesions effectively evade cellular mismatch repair recognition, preserving activity in mismatch-deficient colorectal tumours. Oxaliplatin uniquely produces an acute, cold-triggered **peripheral sensory neuropathy** manifesting as pharyngolaryngeal dysaesthesia, as well as cumulative sensory axonal polyneuropathy with persistent treatment cycles.

left.title: Acute Neuropathy
points: Onset within hours of oxaliplatin infusion
Triggered by cold temperatures or cold drinks

right.title: Cumulative Neuropathy
points: May persist or coast after drug cessation

steps.tx: Oral imidazotetrazine **Temozolomide** undergoes spontaneous non-enzymatic physiological hydrolysis at neutral blood pH to active MTIC. Demonstrating outstanding oral bioavailability, temozolomide crosses the **blood-brain barrier** efficiently, establishing itself as the worldwide standard chemotherapy alongside radiotherapy for newly diagnosed high-grade gliomas. Tumour resistance is mediated by O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase MGMT, where promoter hypermethylation predicts superior temozolomide chemosensitivity.

steps.tx: Bifunctional alkyl sulfonate **Busulfan** covalently crosslinks guanine bases in DNA, exerting potent myeloablative effects on primitive haematopoietic stem cells. Because of this property, busulfan serves as a cornerstone of **conditioning regimens** prior to allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplantation. Critical dose-limiting complications include hepatic sinusoidal obstruction syndrome veno-occlusive disease, seizure activity requiring antiepileptic prophylaxis, and progressive pulmonary interstitial fibrosis.

steps.tx: Late leukaemogenic risks represent a severe delayed complication of **alkylating agents**. Therapy-related myeloid neoplasms characteristically manifest after a latency of 5 to 7 years following exposure to classical alkylating regimens. These therapy-related leukemias typically present with refractory cytopenias, myelodysplastic pre-phases, complex unbalanced karyotypes, and distinctive deletions involving **chromosome 5 or 7**, demonstrating marked resistance to standard induction chemotherapy.
